tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).

Give it a `top` outline with as many points as its footprint (twin for twin, the same way round) and it is lofted straight between the two, or a `lean` (the footprint moved sideways for its top: a sloped mass); the plan then draws the outline at the height it cuts, the section the line where it cuts the skin, 3D a closed skin of triangles, and area, perimeter and volume, per level too, come from the cross sections between the outlines, exactly. `mass_floors` makes a floor at each level it crosses, outlined as the mass is there; the floors hold their mass and level, so running it again updates them instead of doubling them (`prune` deletes the ones on levels the mass no longer crosses; without it they are listed as `stale`). `wall_by_face` (on faces that stand plumb), `floor_by_face` and `roof_by_face` (on the top outline) make a wall on each edge, and a floor and a roof on its top face, and remember their mass and face: `update_by_face` (UF) rebuilds them from the mass as it is now, as Revit's Update to Face does, and refuses the lot, naming each, when a face is gone. The `massfloo 234:| Shaft openings | A hole along an outline from a level (and an offset) up to the next level, a level or a height, cut through every floor, ceiling and roof it reaches into: in 3D, sections, areas and IFC; in plan, its outline and a cross where the plan cuts it, and the hole in a floor seen below | 236:| Rooms | Placed at a point, bounded by the walls and room separation lines around it, and following them when they change; free-standing islands (a shaft) are subtracted; area and perimeter at the wall centre line, or at the walls' faces (`room_area`, as Revit's Area and Volume Computations); IFC spaces carry `Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities`, gross at the centre lines and net at the faces; Revit's Upper Limit, Limit Offset and Base Offset, with Unbounded Height and Volume; frozen rooms keep their boundary and are never recalculated; walls and columns bound rooms while their Room Bounding is on, at the level's Computation Height; two rooms can't share a space (the later is redundant, unbounded); unbounded rooms sit as a 1 m square; Rooms > Reference (the cross) and Room Separation Lines are subcategories; rooms show in 3D as see-through solids when selected, or all of them when a 3D view shows the category | 238:| Structure | Beams, structural columns, isolated footings, wall (strip) footings and structural floors, Revit's Structure tab on the design in [docs/disciplines.md](docs/disciplines.md). A beam, or a wall footing, is a **run**: a straight element from one point to another, of a type with a section (`width` across by `depth` deep, or round) made of a material of the library, at a height over its level (the height of its top, middle or bottom line at each end, so it can slope up to 75°), in a named `system`; a chain of points makes one for each step. A structural column is a column of its own category and types; an isolated footing is a column laid down, its top at the level by default and as thick as `thickness`. A floor says it is `structural`. In plan a run hangs under its level (seen from it, with its centre line dashed to pick it by), crosses the cut plane (in poché) or lies overhead (dashed); a section cuts a rectangular run across its section, and the 3D view draws a sloped prism or, round, a tube; snaps find their ends and middles. Each has a schedule (Id, Type, Level, Length, Width, Depth, with System to group a schedule by), a place in Visibility/Graphics, project parameters and phases, and its IFC class: IfcBeam, IfcColumn, IfcFooting (`PAD_FOOTING`, `STRIP_FOOTING`) and IfcSlab, each with `LoadBearing` in its `Pset_*Common`, swept along its own axis; IFC import reads them back, taking a column or slab whose `Pset_*Common` says it carries load as structural | 239:| Plumbing | Pipes, plumbing fixtures, pipe fittings and pipe accessories, Revit's Plumbing & Piping panel on the same **run** the Structure tab uses. A pipe is round (its `width` its outside diameter) in PVC or copper, at a height over its level at each end (a drain falls, a riser stands upright: the same point twice and two heights), its line the middle unless told, in a named `system` (Água fria, Esgoto) that IFC carries as an `IfcSystem` its pipes are assigned to. A section cuts a pipe in a ring (the poché of a circle, an ellipse when the line is oblique). A fixture is a component of a family whose category says what it is: the project starts with a basin, a WC, a bathtub, a kitchen sink, a shower, a floor drain, elbows, tees and a gate valve, original drawings in the project's language, written to IFC as `IfcSanitaryTerminal`, `IfcWasteTerminal` (`FLOORTRAP`), `IfcPipeFitting` and `IfcValve` and read back into a family of the same category. A family says which fixture or fitting it is (`kind`: `wc`, `lav`, `sink`, `laundry`, `shower`, `bath`…, `floor_drain`, `bend`, `tee`…), which IFC writes as its predefined type (a WC `TOILETPAN`, a basin `WASHHANDBASIN`, an elbow `BEND`) and the import reads back; the starter families say theirs. Fittings and valves are centred on their pipe, so placing one at the pipe's height lines them up; there are no connectors yet | 240:| Electrical | Conduits, cable trays, wires, distribution boards, outlets and switches and luminaires, Revit's Electrical panel on the same run and the same fixtures. A conduit (eletroduto) and a wire are round, a cable tray (eletrocalha) a width by a depth, each at a height over its level at each end (a riser stands upright), in a named `system` (a circuit: Circuito 3) that IFC carries as an `IfcSystem`. The project starts with PVC and steel conduits, perforated trays in three sizes and copper wires, and a distribution board (12, 24 and 36 circuits), a ceiling and a recessed luminaire, an outlet and a switch, each at the mounting height its type says (an outlet's 300, 1100 or 2100 mm to its centre; a luminaire hung from the slab), original drawings in the project's language, the luminaires, outlets and switches carrying connectors (voltage, poles, a load for each type, per phase on a three-phase outlet; `inspect` warns of a device without one), written as `IfcCableCarrierSegment` (`CONDUITSEGMENT`, `CABLETRAYSEGMENT`; a `CABLELADDERSEGMENT` from another tool is read as a tray), `IfcCableSegment`, `IfcElectricDistributionBoard`, `IfcOutlet`, `IfcSwitchingDevice` and `IfcLightFixture`, and read back. The project also keeps Revit's Electrical Settings: voltages (each with the band a device may read within), distribution systems (phases, wires and the voltages each supplies) and wire types (material, insulation, temperature and an ampacity for each section, always in mm²), 241:| Lightning protection (SPDA) | Air terminals (captores), down conductors (condutores de descida), earthing electrodes (hastes de aterramento), inspection boxes and earthing conductors (the ring or mesh), the vocabulary of NBR 5419; Revit has no such tab, so its tools are BIMCraft's own, on the same runs and fixtures. A down conductor is a run that stands upright down a wall (the same point twice and two heights), round in steel or copper or a flat strip; an earthing conductor runs under the level; both belong to a named system. The project starts with a Franklin air terminal in three heights, an earthing rod driven 2.4 or 3 m and a round inspection box, original drawings in the project's language. IFC4 has no lightning protection, so the terminals, rods and boxes are `IfcBuildingElementProxy` of object type `LightningTerminal`, `EarthingRod` and `InspectionBox`, which a reader can filter on and BIMCraft reads back into a family of its category; the conductors are `IfcCableSegment` `CONDUCTORSEGMENT`, told apart by a `Category` BIMCraft writes. A conductor under the level shows in a plan whose view range reaches it (its View Depth) | 242:| Data (lógica, dados e voz) | Data outlets, voice outlets, racks, patch panels, the cable trays of the Electrical tab and structured cabling, the vocabulary of NBR 14565. Cabling is a run like a wire, round, in a named `system` (a link, a network), a Cat6, a Cat6A or an optical cable to start from. The project starts with a data and a voice outlet (a plate with its jacks cut in), a patch panel and a floor rack in three sizes, each at the height its type says, original drawings in the project's language, written as `IfcOutlet` (`DATAOUTLET`, `TELEPHONEOUTLET`), `IfcCommunicationsAppliance` (`NETWORKAPPLIANCE`) and, for the rack, which IFC4 has no class for, an `IfcBuildingElementProxy` of object type `Rack`, and read back into a family of the same category (an `IfcOutlet` of another type is read as a power outlet) | 243:| Reinforcement | `rebar` makes reinforcing bars: a round bar of a diameter (3 to 100 mm) and a steel grade (CA-50 unless told) bent along points in mm, in the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces, which it goes with; `closed` makes a hoop, and `count` with `step` a layer of bars or hoops along a beam. A schedule of rebar lists grade, diameter, length, count and weight (steel at 7850 kg/m³) and, grouped, is a bar schedule. IFC writes and reads each as an `IfcReinforcingBar`, aggregated to its host. The 3D view draws them as tubes (inside their host, so hide it to see them), a section draws the bars it cuts as dots over the poché, and a plan draws each bar of its level as a thin line (solid under the cut plane, dashed over it and under the view range's top, a bar that stands as a dot, bars lying on one another drawn once), hidden with the category. `reinforce` arms a beam, a column, a footing or a floor (round columns and footings, and sloped floors, too) by rules: the engineer gives the cover (or the host's `Cobrimento` parameter) and how many bars, how thick and how far apart (a beam's bars below and above, stirrups with closer ends and hooks, skin bars and anchors; a column's bars on each face, stirrups and ties; a footing's two layers of mesh with their ends turned up; a floor's meshes below and above, stopping short of its outline and openings), and it lays them out inside the cover, checks they fit with room between them and says what to change; a beam's ba 245:| Materials | A library of materials in each project, as Revit's Material Browser: each with a shading colour, a cut pattern and a surface pattern (solid, diagonal, crosshatch, horizontal, vertical, grid, brick, concrete or insulation), drawn in code. Wall, floor, roof and ceiling types are built of layers, each a function, a material from the library and a thickness of its own, adding up to the type's: a wall's from the exterior in, the others' from the top down. Plans and sections cut each layer and hatch it with its material's cut pattern where it's wide enough to hold it (a drafting pattern, the same on screen and on paper); a floor's top in plan and a ceiling's underside in its ceiling plan show their surface pattern at its size in the building; the 3D view shades each layer in its material's colour. A material may have a texture over its colour in the 3D view: a pattern drawn in code (brick, block, boards, concrete, plaster, tile, roof tiles, fabric, metal or insulation, each at its real size) or a picture you add (a PNG or a JPEG, kept in the project, at most 1024 px a side, up to 24 of them), laid on every face of what's made of the material at the size you give it, turned and moved as you say, by the face's own axes (across a wall, a slab's east and north); the library's materials come with theirs. Paint (PT) lays a material, with its texture, over one face of an element, a wall's exterior or a floor's top, over what its type is made of, as Revit's Paint does. A 250:| Linked models | `link` (LK, Manage > Link Model) shows another project, a BIMCraft file or an IFC, as a reference in this one, as Revit's Link Revit does: what it builds (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, columns, beams, stairs, railings, pipes and the other runs, components, masses) is drawn halftone in plans, ceiling plans, sections and the 3D view and written into the images, sheets and PDFs, and the picks snap to it. It can't be selected or edited, and the schedules, the checks and the IFC export never see it, so an architect's model is the base to draw the electrical wiring or the plumbing over. It stands origin to origin, moved and turned as the link says (its Origin and Angle in Properties, or `move` and `rotate` on it; it is picked in the Project Browser's Linked Models group, where a right click reloads or removes it); a level of it at the height of one of the project's stands on that one, the others are named after the link. A project keeps the path (relative to its file where it can be) and reads the file again when it opens, saying which links it couldn't read; Reload All, in the right-click menu of the Project Browser's Linked Models, reads them again. A linked project's own links, views, sheets and annotation stay out. Still to come: shared coordinates, per-view visibility and overrides of a link, hosting on a linked wall, and unloading | 256:| Project parameters | Values of your own that each element of their categories holds (text, numbers, lengths, yes or no, unset a no), as Revit's project parameters are: set in Properties or with `modify`, shown, filtered and sorted in schedules and read by their formulas, and written to IFC in a `Project Parameters` property set and read back from it; renamed, schedules follow; taken off a category, its elements and schedules lose them | 260:| IFC import | IFC2x3 and IFC4 files, as Revit and other BIM tools write them: storeys, straight and curved walls with their doors and windows (cut to a roof over them, attached to it), floors level or sloped and ceilings, with the holes in them, rooms, columns (structural ones, which carry load, in their own category), beams, strip footings, pipes, conduits, cable trays, wires, conductors and cables (runs, found as the longest direction a body spreads in and the section square to it, or, when the body is one profile extruded along anything but up, that way, so a beam shorter than it is deep is still a beam; an upright one running up, with the justification and the `IfcSystem` BIMCraft wrote), isolated footings, structural floors, grids, stairs and ramps of straight flights with the landings between them (a landing slab on its own is a floor), railings (by their axis, or a straight one by its body), roofs flat, sloping all round over any footprint with gable ends, courtyards and openings through them, or one profile swept across, masses (proxies of object type `Mass`, a lofted one with its `BIMCraft_Mass` property set), and the openings through floors, ceilings and roofs (as shafts), each measured from its geometry, whether the file extrudes a profile, writes a Brep or a triangle mesh; material layer sets as their types' layers, stacked from the face the file says, with each material's colour; furniture, sanitary and waste terminals, pipe fittings, valves, distribution bo 261:| Revit files (read only; the command line and the desktop) | A Revit `.rvt` or `.rfa` file of release 2015 to 2027 (checked on Autodesk's sample projects of 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026, and the Snowdon Towers files) is read by a reader of its own, `crates/rvt`, ported in part from [rvt-rs](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs) and fenced by [docs/rvt-provenance.md](docs/rvt-provenance.md). `info` shows its release, build and document GUID, the last save (the saver's name when worksharing records it, and the path it was saved to; shown by `info`, never written into a project or an IFC file), the title, the levels with their names and elevations, and the number of elements in each `BuiltInCategory`, how many of them are placed instances. `run x.rvt`, `convert x.rvt out.ifc` and the MCP server's `open` import the file as a new project: its levels, straight and curved walls with their compound layers and materials (the exterior on the side the file's flip says), floors and ceilings from their sketches (holes and separate loops included), doors and windows in the walls that hold them, columns, rooms with their numbers and names, and roofs (by footprint, those that rise coming in level, and ones by extrusion whose profile is straight lines in a plane square to an axis and whose box the profile and the type's thickness reproduce to a millimetre), converted from feet to millimetres and checked by `Model::check`. Only what a record says is read, and the reply says what is not. Whe 262:| Element ids | Every element, model or annotation, view, sheet or schedule, has an id, six digits from 100000 up, which commands, schedules and the desktop show and take, and a GUID, made once and never changed, as Revit's ElementId and UniqueId: what points at an element (a wall its level, a door its wall, a dimension what it measures, a viewport its view) holds its GUID, so an element that comes in from another file under a new id (Insert from File, `insert`; the same file inserted into itself is copied whole, each copy with a GUID of its own) breaks nothing. IFC writes each element's GUID as its GlobalId and reads it back as one; a file from before GUIDs opens with them, its ids moved up to six digits (1 is 100000). The library has them too: each type, material, picture, family, project parameter, view filter and template, phase, phase filter, design option set and design option has an id (counting down from 999999, so a new project's elements still start at 100000) and a GUID, kept through renames; in a file, whatever names one (a wall's type, a layer's material, a view's template, the phase an element is made in, its values of project parameters, keyed by the parameter's) holds its GUID, so renaming changes nothing in a file but the name. Commands take a library entry by its name or its GUID; `library` lists them, and Insert from File matches them by GUID, then by name. So do their parts: each type's layers and each family's forms and plan symbols hold an id and a G 263:| Files | `.bimcraft` projects (JSON, file format 12: every save is 12, so an earlier build refuses even a plain project saved by this one, saying it is from a newer BIMCraft); IFC4 export with storeys, walls swept up from their plan outline (mitred where they join, an arc in short chords) or, attached to a roof, as closed shells, walls, floors, roofs and ceilings with their material layer sets (each material with its colour), slabs (sloped ones as closed shells), ceilings as coverings, spaces and columns, walls, slabs, doors and windows with their `Qto_*BaseQuantities` (a wall's side area and volume gross and less its openings, a slab's area and volume less its openings), beams (`IfcBeam`), footings (`IfcFooting`), pipes (`IfcPipeSegment`), conduits, cable trays and wires (`IfcCableCarrierSegment`, `IfcCableSegment`) and structural columns and floors, each along its own axis and, if structural, with `LoadBearing` in its `Pset_*Common`, the runs of a system assigned to an `IfcSystem` of its name, stairs and ramps as their flights, landings and railings (each railing with its rail's top line as its axis), roofs as closed shells of flat faces (hip, gable, shed or flat), openings that cut the walls and hold the doors and windows, an opening for each slab, ceiling and roof a shaft passes through, masses as building element proxies of object type `Mass` (a lofted one as a closed face set), and components as furniture, sanitary or waste terminals, pipe fittings, valves, distrib 268:The export writes one type object for each type its walls, slabs, beams, columns, footings, doors, windows, roofs, ceilings, components and runs use (`IfcWallType`, `IfcSlabType`, `IfcBeamType`, `IfcColumnType`, `IfcFootingType`, `IfcDoorType`, `IfcWindowType`, `IfcRoofType`, `IfcCoveringType`, the class each component is written as, and `IfcPipeSegmentType`, `IfcDuctSegmentType`, `IfcCableCarrierSegmentType` and `IfcCableSegmentType`), related to its occurrences by `IfcRelDefinesByType`; strip footings have none yet. Beams and columns carry `Qto_BeamBaseQuantities` and `Qto_ColumnBaseQuantities`. 270:The IFC4 export is checked with [IfcOpenShell](https://ifcopenshell.org) 0.9: the sample house has no schema or EXPRESS rule 275:mirrored chair among it. Import is checked against it too: the sample comes back the same from IFC, element by element, also with its 276:geometry turned into triangle meshes by IfcOpenShell, and a building IfcOpenShell's API writes comes in whole, its roofs 279:twice, one turned, a proxy, a meshed basin) as components where it stood. Project parameters go out as property sets IfcOpenShell 281:IfcOpenShell reads each element's `BIMCraft_Phasing` set and the project's list of phases; they come back from IFC as they went 298:./target/release/bimcraft-cli run --sample --save house.bimcraft --save house.ifc --save plan.png 301:That builds the sample house and saves the project, an IFC4 file and the Level 1 plan: 326:bimcraft-cli run --script house.txt --save house.ifc 327:bimcraft-cli convert building.ifc building.bimcraft # an IFC file from Revit or any BIM tool, as a project 330:bimcraft-cli convert building.rvt building.ifc # a Revit project, imported, then written as IFC4 337:`bimcraft [FILE] [--sample]` opens a `.bimcraft` project, imports an `.ifc` file, or starts on the sample house. The layout 414:| Select by ID, IDs of Selection | Manage > Inquiry, as Revit's, and more. Select by ID takes as many IDs, GUIDs or IFC GlobalIds as you paste (from a schedule, a clash report, an IFC viewer), says as you type what it finds and what nothing has, adds to the selection or replaces it, and opens the plan they are in, zoomed to them. IDs of Selection lists each selected element's category, name, ID, GUID and IFC GlobalId, each selectable, and copies one row, a column (IDs, GUIDs, GlobalIds) or all of it, tab-separated for a spreadsheet | 417:| Files | Ctrl+N, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S; Open takes IFC files too, and a note says what came in and what was left out; the File tab saves, and exports IFC, the sheets as PDF, and the view on screen as PNG (or a plan as SVG) | 446:| `new_model`, `open`, `save` | Projects; `open` imports `.ifc` files, `save` to `.ifc`, `.svg` or `.png` exports | 564:| `point_cloud` | | `path` (a PTS, XYZ, PLY, LAS or E57 scan, or a list of a survey's station files) or `cloud` (one the project holds), `name?`, `level?`, `at?`, `offset?`, `angle?`, `units?` (`m` by default), `spacing?` (one point in each cube that wide), `origin?` (`centre`, its middle on `at` and its foot on the level; or `file`, where its coordinates put it). Drawn in the 3D view, plans and sections, snapped to in plans; IFC export leaves it out | 586:| `new`, `open`, `save` | | projects; `new` takes `name?` and `language?`; `open` imports IFC, listing what it left out; `save` exports by extension |

s, outlets (power, data and telephone), switching devices, communications appliances, light fixtures and proxies (a lightning terminal, an earthing rod, an inspection box or a rack by its object type) as components of families made of their bodies, a family of the category its class says, a family for each family the file names, a type for each type, and a mirror image of a type that type mirrored; project parameters from a `Project Parameters` property set, each of the kind its values are, and from the single values of any other program's property sets (Eberick's `AltoQi_Eberick_*`, `Pset_ConcreteElementGeneral`, `Pset_BeamCommon`), each named for its property, less the characters a formula can't say, with a beam's, column's, footing's or floor's name, where it isn't its type's, as its Mark (V1, P1, L1); phases and design options from a `BIMCraft_Phasing` property set (the project's phases, phase filters, overrides and option sets from the one on the project, each element's phase and option from its own; what the project can't have is left out and listed, and the element stays); walls that nearly meet are joined; a model at map coordinates is moved near the origin; what can't come in is listed, with why |

The IFC4 export is checked with [IfcOpenShell](https://ifcopenshell.org) 0.9: the sample house has no schema or EXPRESS rule
errors, every element builds its geometry, and the walls' volumes (with the openings cut out), the roof's and the slabs' and
ceilings' (with their shafts cut out) match a hand calculation, as do the roofs' of an L-shaped house with a dormer and an
extrusion roof beside it, and of houses round a courtyard, their floors and ceilings open over it too, and of a house of
layered walls, floors, ceilings and roofs, each with its material layer set, and of a flat furnished from the library, a
mirrored chair among it. Import is checked against it too: the sample comes back the same from IFC, element by element, also with its
geometry turned into triangle meshes by IfcOpenShell, and a building IfcOpenShell's API writes comes in whole, its roofs
(slabs per slope, round a courtyard too, or a profile extruded) and its floors and ceilings round a courtyard (a profile with
a void, or a mesh) among it, and its walls' and slabs' layers on the faces their layer sets are stacked from, and its furniture (a stool type placed
twice, one turned, a proxy, a meshed basin) as components where it stood. Project parameters go out as property sets IfcOpenShell
reads back typed as they were (text, a real, a length, a boolean), and come in from a property set its API writes, in metres. A phased sample has no schema or EXPRESS rule errors either, and
IfcOpenShell reads each element's `BIMCraft_Phasing` set and the project's list of phases; they come back from IFC as they went
out, and from a set its API writes (labels and a list value), while a set another tool calls its own, `Phasing` say, is left unread.

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c1'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def furn(f, s, items, name='Stool', at=(0, 0, 0), x=None, cls='IFCFURNITURE', otype=None, kind='Tessellation', pre='NOTDEFINED', tag=None):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, at, (0, 0, 1) if x else None, x)
    body = f.shape(items, kind)
    args = [gid(), None, name, None, otype, lp, f.pds(body), tag]
    if pre is not None:
        args.append(E(pre))
    el = f.add(cls, *args)
    f.contain(s, el)
    return el


def a(f):  # one stool, a box mesh, no type, no style
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    furn(f, s1, [f.mesh_box(-200, -200, 0, 200, 200, 450)])


def b(f):  # an extruded rect
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    furn(f, s1, [f.extrude(f.rect(400, 300), 450)], kind='SweptSolid')


def c(f):  # an L extrusion (non-convex)
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    furn(f, s1, [f.extrude(f.arb([(0, 0), (600, 0), (600, 200), (200, 200), (200, 500), (0, 500)]), 300)], kind='SweptSolid')


def d(f):  # a Brep box
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    furn(f, s1, [f.brep_box(0, 0, 0, 500, 400, 300)], kind='Brep')


def e(f):  # named Family:Type, with a type object of another name
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    el = furn(f, s1, [f.mesh_box(-200, -200, 0, 200, 200, 450)], name='Fam:Typ')
    t = f.add('IFCFURNITURETYPE', gid(), None, 'TypeObj', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('NOTDEFINED'), E('NOTDEFINED'))
    f.rel_type(t, [el])


def g(f):  # Revit style names: Family:Type:123, ObjectType Family:Type, type object Type
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    el = furn(f, s1, [f.mesh_box(-200, -200, 0, 200, 200, 450)], name='Chair-Breuer:Chair-Breuer:123456', otype='Chair-Breuer:Chair-Breuer', tag='123456')
    t = f.add('IFCFURNITURETYPE', gid(), None, 'Chair-Breuer', None, None, None, None, '123457', None, E('NOTDEFINED'), E('NOTDEFINED'))
    f.rel_type(t, [el])


def h(f):  # only a type object
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    el = furn(f, s1, [f.mesh_box(-200, -200, 0, 200, 200, 450)], name=None)
    t = f.add('IFCFURNITURETYPE', gid(), None, 'Stool type', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('NOTDEFINED'), E('NOTDEFINED'))
    f.rel_type(t, [el])


def i(f):  # same name twice, second mirrored in y, third mirrored in x, fourth different
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    P = [(-200, -100, 0), (300, -100, 0), (300, 400, 0), (-200, 400, 0), (-200, -100, 450), (300, -100, 450), (300, 400, 450), (-200, 400, 450)]
    quads = [(0, 3, 2, 1), (4, 5, 6, 7), (0, 1, 5, 4), (1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 0, 4, 7)]
    tris = []
    for q in quads:
        tris.append((q[0], q[1], q[2]))
        tris.append((q[0], q[2], q[3]))
    furn(f, s1, [f.mesh(P, tris)], name='Stool', at=(0, 0, 0))
    Py = [(x, -y, z) for x, y, z in P]
    trisr = [(t[0], t[2], t[1]) for t in tris]
    furn(f, s1, [f.mesh(Py, trisr)], name='Stool', at=(1000, 0, 0))
    Px = [(-x, y, z) for x, y, z in P]
    furn(f, s1, [f.mesh(Px, trisr)], name='Stool', at=(2000, 0, 0))
    P2 = [(x * 2, y, z) for x, y, z in P]
    furn(f, s1, [f.mesh(P2, tris)], name='Stool', at=(3000, 0, 0))
    furn(f, s1, [f.mesh(P, tris)], name='Stool', at=(4000, 0, 0), x=(0, 1, 0))


mk('a_mesh', a)
mk('b_rect', b)
mk('c_L', c)
mk('d_brep', d)
mk('e_named', e)
mk('g_revit', g)
mk('h_typeonly', h)
mk('i_mirror', i)
print(' '.join(out))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""famcats.py GEN.py [filter]: for each generated file, convert with the original and print each
new or changed family's name, category, kind, types and form count (and the reply's skipped)."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import shutil

gen = sys.argv[1]
flt = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
exe = os.environ.get('EXE', '/workspace/executable')
files = subprocess.run(['python3', gen], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
d0 = json.load(open('/tmp/ifc-import-agent/default.bimcraft'))
for f in files:
    if flt and flt not in f:
        continue
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    shutil.copy(f, d)
    name = os.path.basename(f)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', name, '--save', 'o.bimcraft'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print('##', name, p.stdout.strip()[:300], p.stderr.strip()[:200])
    o = os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft')
    if os.path.exists(o):
        j = json.load(open(o))
        for n, fam in j['families'].items():
            f0 = d0['families'].get(n)
            if f0 is not None and json.dumps(f0.get('forms', [])[:1])[:0] == '' and fam.get('forms') and fam['forms'][0].get('mesh') is None and f0 == fam:
                continue
            if f0 is not None and 'mesh' not in json.dumps(fam):
                continue
            print('   ', repr(n), fam['category'], fam.get('kind'), json.dumps(fam.get('parameters')), json.dumps(fam['types']), 'forms', len(fam.get('forms', [])), [k for k in fam if k not in ('category', 'kind', 'parameters', 'types', 'forms')])
    shutil.rmtree(d)

import sys

from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c10'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def furn(f, s, items, name='Stool', at=(0, 0, 0), x=None, cls='IFCFURNITURE', otype=None, kind='Tessellation', pre='NOTDEFINED', tag=None):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, at, (0, 0, 1) if x else None, x)
    body = f.shape(items, kind)
    args = [gid(), None, name, None, otype, lp, f.pds(body), tag]
    if pre is not None:
        args.append(E(pre))
    el = f.add(cls, *args)
    f.contain(s, el)
    return el


def style(f, name, rgb, tr=None):
    c = f.add('IFCCOLOURRGB', None, *[float(v) for v in rgb])
    sh = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLESHADING', c, None if tr is None else float(tr))
    return f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLE', name, E('BOTH'), (sh,))


def material(f, name, st=None):
    m = f.add('IFCMATERIAL', name, None, None)
    if st is not None:
        si = f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', None, (st,), None)
        sr = f.add('IFCSTYLEDREPRESENTATION', f.ctx, 'Style', 'Material', (si,))
        f.add('IFCMATERIALDEFINITIONREPRESENTATION', None, None, (sr,), m)
    return m


def styled(f, item, st):
    f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', item, (st,), None)
    return item


def assoc(f, els, m):
    f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, tuple(els), m)


def box(f, x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1):
    return f.mesh_box(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1)


def t10(f):  # Glass with no transparency in its style; Metal with transparency 0
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    a = style(f, 'Glass', (0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
    b = style(f, 'Metal', (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), 0.0)
    furn(f, s1, [styled(f, box(f, 0, 0, 0, 100, 100, 100), a), styled(f, box(f, 0, 0, 100, 100, 100, 200), b)])


def t11(f):  # style on the mapped item, none inside
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    st = style(f, 'Mapped', (0.1, 0.9, 0.1))
    it = box(f, 0, 0, 0, 100, 100, 100)
    rep = f.add('IFCSHAPEREPRESENTATION', f.body, 'Body', 'Tessellation', (it,))
    rmap = f.add('IFCREPRESENTATIONMAP', f.ax3(), rep)
    op = f.add('IFCCARTESIANTRANSFORMATIONOPERATOR3D', None, None, f.pt(0, 0, 0), None, None)
    mi = f.add('IFCMAPPEDITEM', rmap, op)
    styled(f, mi, st)
    furn(f, s1, [mi], kind='MappedRepresentation')


def t12(f):  # style inside the map, another on the mapped item
    s1, s2 = base(f)
    a = style(f, 'Inner', (0.1, 0.1, 0.9))
    b = style(f, 'Outer', (0.9, 0.1, 0.1))
    it = styled(f, box(f, 0, 0, 0, 100, 100, 100), a)
    it2 = box(f, 0, 0, 100, 100, 100, 200)
    rep = f.add('IFCSHAPEREPRESENTATION', f.body, 'Body', 'Tessellation', (it, it2))
    rmap = f.add('IFCREPRESENTATIONMAP', f.ax3(), rep)
    op = f.add('IFCCARTESIANTRANSFORMATIONOPERATOR3D', None, None, f.pt(0, 0, 0), None, None)
    mi = f.add('IFCMAPPEDITEM', rmap, op)

            b = [p for p in lo if p is not a][0]
            cur.append((tuple(a[:2]), tuple(b[:2])))
        i += 2
        continue

if cur:

    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f, k=1.0):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0 * k)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def wall(f, s, origin, xdir, foot, h, name='W', zbase=0.0):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (origin[0], origin[1], zbase), (0, 0, 1), (xdir[0], xdir[1], 0))
    reps = [f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb(foot), h)])]
    w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(*reps), None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.contain(s, w)
    return w


def far(x, y):
    def fn(f):
        s1, s2 = base(f)
        wall(f, s1, (x, y), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000)
        wall(f, s1, (x, y + 3000), (1, 0), [(0, -100), (5000, -100), (5000, 100), (0, 100)], 3000)
    return fn

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c31'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def model(X, Y):
    def fn(f):
        s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
        s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
        f.close_storeys()
        P = lambda x=0, y=0, z=0: f.lp(s1.lp, (X + x, Y + y, z))
        w1 = wall_rect(f, s1, X, Y, X + 6000, Y, 200, 3000, name='W1')
        wall_rect(f, s1, X + 6000, Y, X + 6000, Y + 4000, 200, 3000, name='W2')
        # floor with a hole and a shaft
        prof = f.arb([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 4000), (0, 4000)], [[(1000, 1000), (2000, 1000), (2000, 2000), (1000, 2000)]])
        sl = f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Floor', None, None, P(0, 0, -200), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(prof, 200)])), None, E('FLOOR'))
        f.contain(s1, sl)
        op = f.add('IFCOPENINGELEMENT', gid(), None, 'Shaft', None, None, P(0, 0, -200), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(4000, 1000), (5000, 1000), (5000, 2000), (4000, 2000)]), 200)])), None, E('OPENING'))
        f.add('IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT', gid(), None, None, None, sl, op)
        # ceiling with a hole
        cprof = f.arb([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 4000), (0, 4000)], [[(3000, 1000), (3500, 1000), (3500, 1500), (3000, 1500)]])
        ce = f.add('IFCCOVERING', gid(), None, 'Ceiling', None, None, P(0, 0, 2600), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(cprof, 20)])), None, E('CEILING'))
        f.contain(s1, ce)
        # a flat roof with an opening (a profile with a void)
        rf = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, 'Roof', None, None, f.lp(s2.lp, (X, Y, 0)), None, None, E('FLAT_ROOF'))
        f.contain(s2, rf)
        rprof = f.arb([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 4000), (0, 4000)], [[(500, 500), (1500, 500), (1500, 1500), (500, 1500)]])
        rs = f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Roof slab', None, None, f.lp(s2.lp, (X, Y, 0)), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(rprof, 300)])), None, E('ROOF'))
        f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, rf, (rs,))
        # a lofted mass
        mp = [(10000, 0, 0), (12000, 0, 0), (12000, 2000, 0), (10000, 2000, 0), (10500, 500, 3000), (11500, 500, 3000), (11500, 1500, 3000), (10500, 1500, 3000)]
        faces = [(0, 3, 2, 1), (4, 5, 6, 7), (0, 1, 5, 4), (1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 0, 4, 7)]
        ms = f.add('IFCBUILDINGELEMENTPROXY', gid(), None, 'Mass', None, 'Mass', P(), f.pds(f.shape([f.brep(mp, faces)], 'Brep')), None, E('USERDEFINED'))
        f.contain(s1, ms)
        f.pset([ms], 'BIMCraft_Mass', {'Loft': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)'})
        # a component, a beam, a column
        fu = f.add('IFCFURNITURE', gid(), None, 'Table:T', None, None, P(3000, 3000, 0), f.pds(f.shape([f.mesh_box(-400, -400, 0, 400, 400, 750)], 'Tessellation')), None, E('NOTDEFINED'))
        f.contain(s1, fu)
        bm = f.add('IFCBEAM', gid(), None, 'B', None, None, P(0, 6000, 2700), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(200, 300), 5000, pos=f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0)))])), None, E('BEAM'))
        f.contain(s1, bm)
        co = f.add('IFCCOLUMN', gid(), None, 'C', None, None, P(8000, 6000, 0), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(300, 300), 3000)])), None, E('COLUMN'))
        f.contain(s1, co)
        # a room
        sp = f.add('IFCSPACE', gid(), None, '1', None, None, P(), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 4000), (0, 4000)]), 2600)])), 'Office', E('ELEMENT'), E('SPACE'), None)
        f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, s1, (sp,))
        # a railing along an axis
        ax = f.shape([f.poly3([(0, 0, 1000), (3000, 0, 1000), (3000, 2000, 1000)])], 'Curve3D', 'Axis')
        bd = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(50, 50, (0, 0)), 1000)])
        ra = f.add('IFCRAILING', gid(), None, 'R', None, None, P(14000, 0, 0), f.pds(ax, bd), None, E('GUARDRAIL'))
        f.contain(s1, ra)
        # a stair
        st = f.add('IFCSTAIR', gid(), None, 'Stair', None, None, P(16000, 0, 0), None, None, E('STRAIGHT_RUN_STAIR'))
        f.contain(s1, st)
        items = [f.extrude(f.rect(280, 900, (140 + i * 280, 0)), 175 * (i + 1)) for i in range(3)]
        fl = f.add('IFCSTAIRFLIGHT', gid(), None, 'Flight', None, None, P(16000, 0, 0), f.pds(f.shape(items)), None, 4, 3, 175.0, 280.0, E('STRAIGHT'))
        f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, st, (fl,))
        # rebar in the beam
        rb = f.add('IFCREINFORCINGBAR', gid(), None, 'Bar', None, None, P(0, 6000, 2700), f.pds(f.shape([f.add('IFCSWEPTDISKSOLID', f.poly3([(50, 0, -100), (4950, 0, -100)]), 8.0, None, None, None)], 'AdvancedSweptSolid')), None, 'CA-50', 16.0, None, None, E('MAIN'), None)
        f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, bm, (rb,))
        # a grid placed far
        a1 = f.add('IFCGRIDAXIS', 'A', f.poly2([(0, -1000), (0, 5000)], close=False), True)
        a2 = f.add('IFCGRIDAXIS', '1', f.poly2([(-1000, 0), (7000, 0)], close=False), True)
        g = f.add('IFCGRID', gid(), None, 'Grid', None, None, P(), None, (a1,), (a2,), None, E('RECTANGULAR'))
        f.contain(s1, g)
        # a door in W1
        o = f.add('IFCOPENINGELEMENT', gid(), None, 'O', None, None, P(1000, 0, 0), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(900, 400, (450, 0)), 2100)])), None, E('OPENING'))
        f.add('IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT', gid(), None, None, None, w1, o)
        d = f.add('IFCDOOR', gid(), None, 'D', None, None, P(1000, 0, 0), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(900, 50, (450, 0)), 2100)])), None, 2100.0, 900.0, E('DOOR'), E('SINGLE_SWING_LEFT'), None)
        f.add('IFCRELFILLSELEMENT', gid(), None, None, None, o, d)
        f.contain(s1, d)
        # a room separation line
        vs = f.add('IFCVIRTUALELEMENT', gid(), None, 'Sep', None, 'RoomSeparation', P(), f.pds(f.shape([f.poly3([(3000, 0), (3000, 4000)])], 'Curve3D', 'Axis')), None)
        f.contain(s1, vs)
        # a pipe and a sloped floor
        pp = f.add('IFCPIPESEGMENT', gid(), None, 'P', None, None, P(0, 8000, 500), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.add('IFCCIRCLEPROFILEDEF', E('AREA'), None, f.ax2(), 50.0), 3000, pos=f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0)))])), None, E('RIGIDSEGMENT'))
        f.contain(s1, pp)
        sp_ = [(20000, 0, 0), (24000, 0, 400), (24000, 3000, 400), (20000, 3000, 0), (20000, 0, -200), (24000, 0, 200), (24000, 3000, 200), (20000, 3000, -200)]
        faces = [(0, 1, 2, 3), (4, 7, 6, 5), (0, 4, 5, 1), (1, 5, 6, 2), (2, 6, 7, 3), (3, 7, 4, 0)]
        sf = f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Sloped', None, None, P(), f.pds(f.shape([f.brep(sp_, faces)], 'Brep')), None, E('FLOOR'))
        f.contain(s1, sf)
        # a ramp
        prof = f.arb([(0, 0), (3000, 300), (3000, 400), (0, 100)])
        solid = f.extrude(prof, 1200, pos=f.ax3((0, 600, 0), (0, -1, 0), (1, 0, 0)))
        rp2 = f.add('IFCRAMP', gid(), None, 'RampBody', None, None, P(0, 12000, 0), f.pds(f.shape([solid])), None, E('STRAIGHT_RUN_RAMP'))
        f.contain(s1, rp2)
    return fn


for name, X, Y in [('near', 0, 0), ('far', 250000000, 150000000)]:
    f = F('IFC4', 'mm')
    f.header()
    model(X, Y)(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))
print(' '.join(out))

"""The asset IFC files, their site (or building) placed 250 km east and 150 km north."""
import glob
import os
import re

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c32'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob('/workspace/assets/**/*.ifc', recursive=True)):
    text = open(f, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    lines = text.split('\n')
    ents = {}
    for l in lines:
        m = re.match(r'#(\d+)=([A-Z0-9]+)\((.*)\);\s*$', l)
        if m:
            ents[int(m.group(1))] = (m.group(2), m.group(3))
    # the site's placement → its axis placement → its point
    site = [k for k, v in ents.items() if v[0] == 'IFCSITE']
    if not site:
        continue
    args = ents[site[0]][1]
    refs = re.findall(r'#(\d+)', args)
    lp = None
    for r in refs:
        if ents.get(int(r), ('',))[0] == 'IFCLOCALPLACEMENT':
            lp = int(r)
            break
    if lp is None:
        continue
    ax = int(re.findall(r'#(\d+)', ents[lp][1])[-1])
    pt = int(re.findall(r'#(\d+)', ents[ax][1])[0])
    # the point may be shared: write a new one
    unit_m = 'METRE.)' in text and '.MILLI.' not in text
    X, Y = (250000.0, 150000.0) if unit_m else (250000000.0, 150000000.0)
    new_id = max(ents) + 1
    new_line = '#%d=IFCCARTESIANPOINT((%r,%r,0.));' % (new_id, X, Y)
    new_lines = []
    for l in lines:
        if l.startswith('#%d=' % ax):
            l = l.replace('#%d' % pt, '#%d' % new_id, 1) if False else re.sub(r'\(#%d,' % pt, '(#%d,' % new_id, l, count=1)
        new_lines.append(l)
        if l.startswith('DATA;'):
            new_lines.append(new_line)
    name = f.replace('/workspace/assets/', '').replace('/', '__')
    p = os.path.join(D, name)
    open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(new_lines))
    out.append(p)
print(' '.join(out))

    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def run(f, s, cls, a, b, z, prof, name='X', pt=None, ext_x=None):
    """extrusion from a to b (plan) at height z of the profile centre"""
    dx, dy = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]
    L = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    lp = f.lp(s.lp, (a[0], a[1], z))
    pos = f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (dx / L, dy / L, 0), ext_x or (-dy / L, dx / L, 0))
    body = f.shape([f.extrude(prof, L, pos)])
    args = [gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(body), None]
    if pt:
        args.append(E(pt))
    el = f.add(cls, *args)
    f.contain(s, el)
    return el

import sys
import math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from roompt2 import cases


def cross(o, a, b):
    return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])


def inside(p, a, b, c):
    # strictly or on edge?
    d1 = cross(a, b, p)
    d2 = cross(b, c, p)
    d3 = cross(c, a, p)
    return d1 >= 0 and d2 >= 0 and d3 >= 0


def signed(pts):
    return sum(pts[i][0] * pts[(i + 1) % len(pts)][1] - pts[(i + 1) % len(pts)][0] * pts[i][1] for i in range(len(pts))) / 2


def earclip(pts, restart):
    v = list(pts)
    tris = []
    i = 0
    guard = 0
    while len(v) > 3 and guard < 10000:
        guard += 1
        n = len(v)
        found = False
        for k in range(n):
            j = (i + k) % n
            a, b, c = v[(j - 1) % n], v[j], v[(j + 1) % n]
            if cross(a, b, c) <= 0:
                continue
            ok = True
            for q in v:
                if q in (a, b, c):
                    continue
                if inside(q, a, b, c):
                    ok = False
                    break
            if ok:
                tris.append((a, b, c))
                del v[j]
                i = 0 if restart else j % len(v)
                found = True
                break
        if not found:
            break
    if len(v) == 3:
        tris.append(tuple(v))
    return tris


def area(t):
    (a, b, c) = t
    return abs(cross(a, b, c)) / 2

"""A small building with a bit of everything, the way BIM tools write one."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c48'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def material(f, name, rgb):
    m = f.add('IFCMATERIAL', name, None, None)
    c = f.add('IFCCOLOURRGB', None, *[float(v) for v in rgb])
    sh = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLESHADING', c, None)
    st = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLE', name, E('BOTH'), (sh,))
    si = f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', None, (st,), None)
    sr = f.add('IFCSTYLEDREPRESENTATION', f.ctx, 'Style', 'Material', (si,))
    f.add('IFCMATERIALDEFINITIONREPRESENTATION', None, None, (sr,), m)
    return m, st


def building(f, units):
    k = 1.0 if units == 'mm' else 0.001
    L = lambda v: v * k
    storeys = [f.storey('Ground', 0.0), f.storey('First', L(3000.0)), f.storey('Roof', L(6000.0))]
    f.close_storeys()
    brick, brick_st = material(f, 'Brick', (0.7, 0.3, 0.2))
    ins, _ = material(f, 'Insulation', (0.9, 0.9, 0.5))
    block, _ = material(f, 'Concrete block', (0.6, 0.6, 0.6))
    plaster, _ = material(f, 'Plaster', (0.95, 0.95, 0.9))
    conc, _ = material(f, 'Concrete', (0.7, 0.7, 0.7))
    oak, oak_st = material(f, 'Oak', (0.6, 0.4, 0.2))
    layers = [f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYER', m, L(t), None, None, None, None, None) for m, t in [(brick, 100), (ins, 50), (block, 150)]]
    ext_set = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSET', tuple(layers), 'Exterior 300', None)
    int_layer = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYER', plaster, L(100), None, None, None, None, None)
    int_set = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSET', (int_layer,), 'Interior 100', None)
    ext_type = f.add('IFCWALLTYPE', gid(), None, 'Exterior - 300mm', None, None, None, None, None, E('STANDARD'))
    int_type = f.add('IFCWALLTYPE', gid(), None, 'Interior - 100mm', None, None, None, None, None, E('STANDARD'))
    f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (ext_type,), ext_set)
    f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (int_type,), int_set)
    W, Hh = 12000, 8000
    ext_walls = []
    int_walls = []
    for si, s in enumerate(storeys[:2]):
        corners = [(0, 0), (W, 0), (W, Hh), (0, Hh)]
        for i in range(4):
            a, b = corners[i], corners[(i + 1) % 4]
            dx, dy = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]
            ln = math.hypot(dx, dy)
            lp = f.lp(s.lp, (L(a[0]), L(a[1]), 0), (0, 0, 1), (dx / ln, dy / ln, 0))
            body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(L(ln), L(300), (L(ln / 2), L(-150))), L(3000))])
            ax = f.shape([f.poly2([(0, 0), (L(ln), 0)], close=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis')
            w = f.add('IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE', gid(), None, 'Basic Wall:Exterior - 300mm:%d' % (1000 + si * 10 + i), None, 'Basic Wall:Exterior - 300mm', lp, f.pds(ax, body), str(1000 + si * 10 + i), E('STANDARD'))
            f.contain(s, w)
            f.rel_type(ext_type, [w])
            usage = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSETUSAGE', ext_set, E('AXIS2'), E('NEGATIVE'), 0.0, None)
            f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (w,), usage)
            ext_walls.append((si, i, w, a, (dx / ln, dy / ln), ln))
        # an interior wall across
        lp = f.lp(s.lp, (L(6000), L(-150), 0), (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0))
        body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(L(7700), L(100), (L(3850), 0)), L(3000))])
        ax = f.shape([f.poly2([(0, 0), (L(7700), 0)], close=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis')
        wi = f.add('IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE', gid(), None, 'Basic Wall:Interior - 100mm:%d' % (2000 + si), None, None, lp, f.pds(ax, body), str(2000 + si), E('STANDARD'))
        f.contain(s, wi)
        f.rel_type(int_type, [wi])
        usage = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSETUSAGE', int_set, E('AXIS2'), E('POSITIVE'), L(-50.0), None)
        f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (wi,), usage)
        int_walls.append(wi)
    # doors in the front walls and the interior walls, windows in the back walls
    door_type = f.add('IFCDOORTYPE', gid(), None, 'M_Single-Flush:0915 x 2134mm', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('DOOR'), E('SINGLE_SWING_LEFT'), None, None)
    win_type = f.add('IFCWINDOWTYPE', gid(), None, 'M_Fixed:0915 x 1220mm', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('WINDOW'), E('SINGLE_PANEL'), None, None)
    tagn = 300
    for si, i, w, a, d, ln in ext_walls:
        if i not in (0, 2):
            continue
        for k, off in enumerate([2000, 8000]):
            x, y = a[0] + d[0] * off, a[1] + d[1] * off
            s = storeys[si]
            isdoor = (i == 0 and si == 0 and k == 0)
            ww, hh, sill = (915, 2134, 0) if isdoor else (915, 1220, 900)
            olp = f.lp(s.lp, (L(x), L(y), L(sill)), (0, 0, 1), (d[0], d[1], 0))
            o = f.add('IFCOPENINGELEMENT', gid(), None, 'Opening', None, None, olp, f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(L(ww), L(600), (L(ww / 2), L(-150))), L(hh))])), None, E('OPENING'))
            f.add('IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT', gid(), None, None, None, w, o)
            elp = f.lp(s.lp, (L(x), L(y), L(sill)), (0, 0, 1), (d[0], d[1], 0))
            body = f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(L(ww), L(50), (L(ww / 2), L(-150))), L(hh))])
            tagn += 1
            if isdoor:
                el = f.add('IFCDOOR', gid(), None, 'M_Single-Flush:0915 x 2134mm:%d' % tagn, None, 'M_Single-Flush:0915 x 2134mm', elp, f.pds(body), str(tagn), L(hh), L(ww), E('DOOR'), E('SINGLE_SWING_LEFT'), None)
                f.rel_type(door_type, [el])
            else:
                el = f.add('IFCWINDOW', gid(), None, 'M_Fixed:0915 x 1220mm:%d' % tagn, None, 'M_Fixed:0915 x 1220mm', elp, f.pds(body), str(tagn), L(hh), L(ww), E('WINDOW'), E('SINGLE_PANEL'), None)
                f.rel_type(win_type, [el])
            f.add('IFCRELFILLSELEMENT', gid(), None, None, None, o, el)
            f.contain(s, el)
    # floors with a stair opening; a roof slab
    fl_type = f.add('IFCSLABTYPE', gid(), None, 'Floor:Generic 200mm', None, None, None, None, None, E('FLOOR'))
    for si, s in enumerate(storeys[:2]):
        prof = f.arb([(0, 0), (L(W), 0), (L(W), L(Hh)), (0, L(Hh))])
        sl = f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Floor:Generic 200mm:%d' % (4000 + si), None, None, f.lp(s.lp, (0, 0, L(-200))), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(prof, L(200))])), str(4000 + si), E('FLOOR'))
        f.contain(s, sl)
        f.rel_type(fl_type, [sl])
        f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (sl,), conc)
        if si == 1:
            op = f.add('IFCOPENINGELEMENT', gid(), None, 'Shaft', None, None, f.lp(s.lp, (0, 0, L(-200))), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(L(1000), L(1000)), (L(2200), L(1000)), (L(2200), L(4000)), (L(1000), L(4000))]), L(200))])), None, E('OPENING'))
            f.add('IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT', gid(), None, None, None, sl, op)
    rf = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, 'Basic Roof:Generic - 300mm:5000', None, None, f.lp(storeys[2].lp), None, '5000', E('FLAT_ROOF'))
    f.contain(storeys[2], rf)
    rs = f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Basic Roof:Generic - 300mm:5001', None, None, f.lp(storeys[2].lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(0, 0), (L(W), 0), (L(W), L(Hh)), (0, L(Hh))]), L(300))])), None, E('ROOF'))
    f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, rf, (rs,))
    # spaces
    for si, s in enumerate(storeys[:2]):
        for j, (x0, x1, nm) in enumerate([(0, 6000, 'Living'), (6000, W, 'Kitchen')]):
            sp = f.add('IFCSPACE', gid(), None, '%d0%d' % (si + 1, j + 1), None, None, f.lp(s.lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.arb([(L(x0 + 150), L(150)), (L(x1 - 150), L(150)), (L(x1 - 150), L(Hh - 150)), (L(x0 + 150), L(Hh - 150))]), L(2600))])), nm, E('ELEMENT'), E('INTERNAL'), None)
            f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, s, (sp,))
    # furniture: a mapped table type placed three times, one turned
    it = f.mesh_box(L(-800), L(-450), 0, L(800), L(450), L(750))
    f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', it, (oak_st,), None)
    rep = f.add('IFCSHAPEREPRESENTATION', f.body, 'Body', 'Tessellation', (it,))
    rmap = f.add('IFCREPRESENTATIONMAP', f.ax3(), rep)
    tt = f.add('IFCFURNITURETYPE', gid(), None, 'Table-Dining:1600x900', None, None, None, (rmap,), None, None, E('TABLE'), E('NOTDEFINED'))
    tabs = []
    for (x, y, ang) in [(3000, 4000, 0), (9000, 4000, 90), (3000, 4000, 30)]:
        s = storeys[0] if len(tabs) < 2 else storeys[1]
        a = math.radians(ang)
        op = f.add('IFCCARTESIANTRANSFORMATIONOPERATOR3D', None, None, f.pt(0, 0, 0), None, None)
        mi = f.add('IFCMAPPEDITEM', rmap, op)
        el = f.add('IFCFURNITURE', gid(), None, 'Table-Dining:1600x900:%d' % (6000 + len(tabs)), None, 'Table-Dining:1600x900', f.lp(s.lp, (L(x), L(y), 0), (0, 0, 1), (math.cos(a), math.sin(a), 0)), f.pds(f.shape([mi], 'MappedRepresentation')), str(6000 + len(tabs)), E('TABLE'))
        f.contain(s, el)
        tabs.append(el)
    f.rel_type(tt, tabs)
    # columns and a beam on the first floor
    for x in (4000, 8000):
        c = f.add('IFCCOLUMN', gid(), None, 'Concrete-Rectangular-Column:300 x 450mm:%d' % (7000 + x), None, 'Concrete-Rectangular-Column:300 x 450mm', f.lp(storeys[1].lp, (L(x), L(4000), 0)), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(L(300), L(450)), L(3000))])), str(7000 + x), E('COLUMN'))
        f.contain(storeys[1], c)
        f.pset([c], 'Pset_ColumnCommon', {'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)'})
    bm = f.add('IFCBEAM', gid(), None, 'Concrete-Rectangular Beam:300x600mm:8000', None, 'Concrete-Rectangular Beam:300x600mm', f.lp(storeys[1].lp, (L(4000), L(4000), L(2700))), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.rect(L(300), L(600)), L(4000), pos=f.ax3((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0)))])), '8000', E('BEAM'))
    f.contain(storeys[1], bm)
    # a stair from ground to first in the shaft
    st = f.add('IFCSTAIR', gid(), None, 'Stair', None, None, f.lp(storeys[0].lp, (L(1000), L(1000), 0)), None, '9000', E('STRAIGHT_RUN_STAIR'))
    f.contain(storeys[0], st)
    items = [f.extrude(f.rect(L(1200), L(280), (L(600), L(140 + i * 280))), L(176.47 * (i + 1))) for i in range(10)]
    fl = f.add('IFCSTAIRFLIGHT', gid(), None, 'Run', None, None, f.lp(storeys[0].lp, (L(1000), L(1000), 0)), f.pds(f.shape(items)), None, 17, 16, L(176.47), L(280.0), E('STRAIGHT'))
    f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, st, (fl,))
    # unsupported things
    for i in range(3):
        f.contain(storeys[0], f.add('IFCAIRTERMINAL', gid(), None, 'Diffuser', None, None, f.lp(storeys[0].lp, (L(1000 + i * 1000), L(7000), L(2700))), f.pds(f.shape([f.mesh_box(0, 0, 0, L(300), L(300), L(50))], 'Tessellation')), None, E('DIFFUSER')))
    f.pset([ext_walls[0][2]], 'Pset_WallCommon', {'IsExternal': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)', 'FireRating': "IFCLABEL('60 min')", 'LoadBearing': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)'})


for units in ('mm', 'm'):
    f = F('IFC4', units)
    f.header('House')
    building(f, units)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, 'house_%s.ifc' % units)))
    f = F('IFC2X3', units)
    f.header('House')
    building(f, units)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, 'house_2x3_%s.ifc' % units)))
print(' '.join(out))

    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)

    L = math.hypot(dx, dy)

"""A building the way IfcOpenShell's API writes one: metres, indexed polycurves, layer set usages
on types, a slab per roof slope, a courtyard profile with a void, a mesh ceiling, typed furniture
mapped twice (one turned), a proxy, a meshed basin, project parameters in metres."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/components/c65'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def ipc(f, pts, closed=True):
    pl = f.add('IFCCARTESIANPOINTLIST2D', tuple((float(x), float(y)) for x, y in pts))
    n = len(pts)
    idx = list(range(1, n + 1)) + ([1] if closed else [])
    return f.add('IFCINDEXEDPOLYCURVE', pl, (Raw('IFCLINEINDEX((%s))' % ','.join(str(i) for i in idx)),), False)


def iprof(f, pts, voids=None):
    if voids:
        return f.add('IFCARBITRARYPROFILEDEFWITHVOIDS', E('AREA'), None, ipc(f, pts), tuple(ipc(f, v) for v in voids))
    return f.add('IFCARBITRARYCLOSEDPROFILEDEF', E('AREA'), None, ipc(f, pts))


def material(f, name, rgb):
    m = f.add('IFCMATERIAL', name, None, 'Category')
    c = f.add('IFCCOLOURRGB', name, *[float(v) for v in rgb])
    sh = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLESHADING', c, 0.0)
    st = f.add('IFCSURFACESTYLE', name, E('BOTH'), (sh,))
    si = f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', None, (st,), None)
    sr = f.add('IFCSTYLEDREPRESENTATION', f.ctx, 'Body', None, (si,))
    f.add('IFCMATERIALDEFINITIONREPRESENTATION', None, None, (sr,), m)
    return m, st


def building(f):
    s1 = f.storey('Ground Floor', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('First Floor', 3.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    conc, conc_st = material(f, 'Concrete', (0.75, 0.75, 0.75))
    brick, _ = material(f, 'Brick', (0.7, 0.35, 0.25))
    wood, wood_st = material(f, 'Wood', (0.6, 0.45, 0.3))
    ceramic, cer_st = material(f, 'Ceramic', (0.95, 0.95, 0.95))
    # wall type with a layer set; walls with usages
    l1 = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYER', brick, 0.1, None, 'Brick', None, 'Finish', None)
    l2 = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYER', conc, 0.15, None, 'Core', None, 'LoadBearing', None)
    wset = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSET', (l1, l2), 'WAL250', None)
    wt = f.add('IFCWALLTYPE', gid(), None, 'WAL250', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('SOLIDWALL'))
    f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (wt,), wset)
    walls = []
    pts = [(0, 0), (12, 0), (12, 10), (0, 10)]
    for i in range(4):
        a, b = pts[i], pts[(i + 1) % 4]
        dx, dy = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]
        ln = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        lp = f.lp(s1.lp, (a[0], a[1], 0.0), (0, 0, 1), (dx / ln, dy / ln, 0))
        ax = f.shape([ipc(f, [(0, 0), (ln, 0)], closed=False)], 'Curve2D', 'Axis')
        body = f.shape([f.extrude(iprof(f, [(0, 0), (ln, 0), (ln, 0.25), (0, 0.25)]), 3.0)])
        w = f.add('IFCWALL', gid(), None, 'Wall %d' % (i + 1), None, None, lp, f.pds(ax, body), None, E('SOLIDWALL'))
        f.contain(s1, w)
        u = f.add('IFCMATERIALLAYERSETUSAGE', wset, E('AXIS2'), E('POSITIVE'), 0.0, None)
        f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (w,), u)
        walls.append(w)
    f.rel_type(wt, walls)
    # a slab round a courtyard (a profile with a void), and a ceiling as a mesh with a hole
    st_ = f.add('IFCSLABTYPE', gid(), None, 'SLAB200', None, None, None, None, None, None, E('FLOOR'))
    sl = f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Slab', None, None, f.lp(s2.lp, (0, 0, -0.2)), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(iprof(f, [(0, 0), (12, 0), (12, 10), (0, 10)], [[(4, 3), (8, 3), (8, 7), (4, 7)]]), 0.2)])), None, E('FLOOR'))
    f.contain(s2, sl)
    f.rel_type(st_, [sl])
    f.add('IFCRELASSOCIATESMATERIAL', gid(), None, None, None, (sl,), conc)
    P = [(0, 0, 2.7), (12, 0, 2.7), (12, 10, 2.7), (0, 10, 2.7), (4, 3, 2.7), (8, 3, 2.7), (8, 7, 2.7), (4, 7, 2.7)]
    P += [(x, y, 2.68) for x, y, z in P]
    tris = []
    ring = [(0, 1, 5, 4), (1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 0, 4, 7)]
    for a_, b_, c_, d_ in ring:
        tris += [(a_, b_, c_), (a_, c_, d_)]
        tris += [(a_ + 8, c_ + 8, b_ + 8), (a_ + 8, d_ + 8, c_ + 8)]
    for i in range(4):
        j = (i + 1) % 4
        tris += [(i, i + 8, j + 8), (i, j + 8, j)]
        tris += [(i + 4, j + 4, j + 12), (i + 4, j + 12, i + 12)]
    ce = f.add('IFCCOVERING', gid(), None, 'Ceiling', None, None, f.lp(s1.lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.mesh(P, tris)], 'Tessellation')), None, E('CEILING'))
    f.contain(s1, ce)
    # a roof: a slab per slope (a gable)
    rf = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, 'Roof', None, None, f.lp(s2.lp), None, None, E('GABLE_ROOF'))
    f.contain(s2, rf)
    parts = []
    for sgn in (1, -1):
        y0 = 0 if sgn == 1 else 10
        prof = iprof(f, [(0, 0), (12, 0), (12, 5.0 / math.cos(math.radians(30))), (0, 5.0 / math.cos(math.radians(30)))])
        a = math.radians(30)
        if sgn == 1:
            pos = f.ax3((0, 0, 3.0), (0, -math.sin(a), math.cos(a)), (1, 0, 0))
        else:
            pos = f.ax3((12, 10, 3.0), (0, math.sin(a), math.cos(a)), (-1, 0, 0))
        parts.append(f.add('IFCSLAB', gid(), None, 'Roof slope', None, None, f.lp(s2.lp), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(prof, 0.25, pos=pos)])), None, E('ROOF')))
    f.add('IFCRELAGGREGATES', gid(), None, None, None, rf, tuple(parts))
    # furniture: a stool type mapped twice, one turned; a proxy; a meshed basin
    it = f.mesh_box(-0.2, -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.2, 0.45)
    f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', it, (wood_st,), None)
    rep = f.add('IFCSHAPEREPRESENTATION', f.body, 'Body', 'Tessellation', (it,))
    rmap = f.add('IFCREPRESENTATIONMAP', f.ax3(), rep)
    stool_t = f.add('IFCFURNITURETYPE', gid(), None, 'Stool', None, None, None, (rmap,), None, None, E('CHAIR'), E('NOTDEFINED'))
    stools = []
    for k, (x, y, ang) in enumerate([(2, 2, 0), (3, 2, 45)]):
        a = math.radians(ang)
        op = f.add('IFCCARTESIANTRANSFORMATIONOPERATOR3D', None, None, f.pt(0, 0, 0), None, None)
        mi = f.add('IFCMAPPEDITEM', rmap, op)
        f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', mi, (wood_st,), None)
        el = f.add('IFCFURNITURE', gid(), None, 'Stool', None, None, f.lp(s1.lp, (x, y, 0), (0, 0, 1), (math.cos(a), math.sin(a), 0)), f.pds(f.shape([mi], 'MappedRepresentation')), None, E('CHAIR'))
        f.contain(s1, el)
        stools.append(el)
    f.rel_type(stool_t, stools)
    px = f.add('IFCBUILDINGELEMENTPROXY', gid(), None, 'Planter', None, None, f.lp(s1.lp, (5, 5, 0)), f.pds(f.shape([f.extrude(f.add('IFCCIRCLEPROFILEDEF', E('AREA'), None, f.ax2(), 0.3), 0.6)])), None, E('ELEMENT'))
    f.contain(s1, px)
    bP = [(0, 0, 0.8), (0.5, 0, 0.8), (0.5, 0.4, 0.8), (0, 0.4, 0.8), (0.1, 0.1, 0.7), (0.4, 0.1, 0.7), (0.4, 0.3, 0.7), (0.1, 0.3, 0.7)]
    pl = f.add('IFCCARTESIANPOINTLIST3D', tuple(tuple(float(c) for c in p) for p in bP))
    faces = [f.add('IFCINDEXEDPOLYGONALFACE', idx) for idx in [(1, 2, 6, 5), (2, 3, 7, 6), (3, 4, 8, 7), (4, 1, 5, 8), (5, 6, 7, 8)]]
    basin_item = f.add('IFCPOLYGONALFACESET', pl, True, tuple(faces), None)
    f.add('IFCSTYLEDITEM', basin_item, (cer_st,), None)
    basin = f.add('IFCSANITARYTERMINAL', gid(), None, 'Basin', None, None, f.lp(s1.lp, (10, 1, 0)), f.pds(f.shape([basin_item], 'Tessellation')), None, E('WASHHANDBASIN'))
    f.contain(s1, basin)
    # project parameters as IfcOpenShell writes them, in metres
    f.pset([walls[0]], 'Project Parameters', {'Fire Rating': "IFCLABEL('REI 60')", 'Acoustic Rating': 'IFCREAL(52.0)', 'Cover': 'IFCLENGTHMEASURE(0.025)', 'Rated': 'IFCBOOLEAN(.T.)'})
    f.pset([walls[0]], 'BIMCraft_Phasing', {'Phase Created': "IFCLABEL('Existing')"})


f = F('IFC4', 'm')
f.header('IfcOpenShell building')
building(f)
out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, 'ios.ifc')))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ifc-import-agent')
from ifcgen import *
import os
import math

D = '/tmp/ifc-import-agent/roofs/r7'
os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
out = []


def mk(name, fn, units='mm', schema='IFC4'):
    f = F(schema, units)
    f.header()
    fn(f)
    out.append(f.save(os.path.join(D, name + '.ifc')))


def base(f):
    s1 = f.storey('L1', 0.0)
    s2 = f.storey('L2', 3000.0)
    f.close_storeys()
    return s1, s2


def roof_brep(f, s, solids, name='R'):
    lp = f.lp(s.lp)
    items = [f.brep(P, F_) for P, F_ in solids]
    r = f.add('IFCROOF', gid(), None, name, None, None, lp, f.pds(f.shape(items, 'Brep')), None, E('HIP_ROOF'))
    f.contain(s, r)
    return r


def pyramid_shell(deg, w=6000, t=300):
    """a constant-thickness pyramid: top and underside parallel, vertical edges at the eaves"""
    c = w / 2
    h = c * math.tan(math.radians(deg))
    tv = t / math.cos(math.radians(deg))
    P = [(0, 0, tv), (w, 0, tv), (w, w, tv), (0, w, tv), (c, c, tv + h), (0, 0, 0), (w, 0, 0), (w, w, 0), (0, w, 0), (c, c, h)]
    faces = [(0, 1, 4), (1, 2, 4), (2, 3, 4), (3, 0, 4), (5, 9, 6), (6, 9, 7), (7, 9, 8), (8, 9, 5), (5, 6, 1, 0), (6, 7, 2, 1), (7, 8, 3, 2), (8, 5, 0, 3)]
    return [(P, faces)]


def pyramid_split(deg, w=6000, t=300):
    """the same, as four solids, one per slope"""
    c = w / 2
    h = c * math.tan(math.radians(deg))
    tv = t / math.cos(math.radians(deg))
    corners = [(0, 0), (w, 0), (w, w), (0, w)]
    sols = []
    for i in range(4):
        a, b = corners[i], corners[(i + 1) % 4]
        P = [(a[0], a[1], 0), (b[0], b[1], 0), (c, c, h), (a[0], a[1], tv), (b[0], b[1], tv), (c, c, h + tv)]
        faces = [(0, 2, 1), (3, 4, 5), (0, 1, 4, 3), (1, 2, 5, 4), (2, 0, 3, 5)]
        sols.append((P, faces))
    return sols


for deg in [0.5, 1, 1.15, 1.5, 2, 5, 10, 30]:
    mk('shell_%s' % str(deg).replace('.', 'p'), lambda f, deg=deg: (base(f), roof_brep(f, f.storeys[1], pyramid_shell(deg))))
    mk('split_%s' % str(deg).replace('.', 'p'), lambda f, deg=deg: (base(f), roof_brep(f, f.storeys[1], pyramid_split(deg))))
print(' '.join(out))

    cases.append(('cut%d' % deg, T30, 300.0, (run, 0.0), 0.0, want))
for name, tn, eave_top, low, lev, want in cases:
    s = math.atan(tn)
    ztop = eave_top + low[0] * tn

import math


def r2(x):
    return round(x * 100) / 100


def r3(x):
    return round(x * 1000) / 1000


T30 = math.tan(math.radians(30))
cases = []
# e_eaves45: top from (0, t) rising 2886.75 over 5000; lowest point (t, 0); eave top t
t = 288.68
cases.append(('e45', 2886.75 / 5000, t, (t, 0.0), 0.0, 288.671))
# g_cut_low
cases.append(('gcut', 2886.75 / 5000, t - 300, (t, -300.0), 0.0, 808.287))
# cut series (gen70): h = 300, run = h / tan(deg); top from (0, h) rising 5000*T30 over 5000
for deg, want in [(35, 428.445), (40, 357.525), (44, 310.665), (46, 289.705), (50, 251.725), (60, 173.205), (80, 52.905)]:
    run = 300.0 / math.tan(math.radians(deg))
    cases.append(('cut%d' % deg, T30, 300.0, (run, 0.0), 0.0, want))
for name, tn, eave_top, low, lev, want in cases:
    s = math.atan(tn)
    ztop = eave_top + low[0] * tn
    vert0 = ztop - low[1]
    for vs in ('s', 'r2s'):
        for ts in ('s', 'r2s'):
            sl_v = s if vs == 's' else math.radians(r2(math.degrees(s)))
            sl_t = s if ts == 's' else math.radians(r2(math.degrees(s)))
            th = r2(vert0 * math.cos(s))
            vertical = th / math.cos(sl_v)
            e = eave_top - vertical - lev
            oh = r3(-e / math.tan(sl_t))
            mark = 'OK' if abs(oh - want) < 1e-9 else '--'
            print(name, vs, ts, th, oh, want, mark)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms
